newsitem.title: ANGOLA: ELF says testing promising Angolan well. [CORRECTED 18:03 GMT]
newsitem.headline: ELF says testing promising Angolan well. [CORRECTED 18:03 GMT]

text.p: Elf Exploration Angola said it was test drilling a promising oil find in a deepwater field off Angola and results could be known as early as March.
"We hope to complete the test well by the end of February," Elf's director general in Angola, Patrick Timbart, told Reuters at the weekend.
"Afterwards there will be some analysis that should take two to three weeks. We will know just how good this discovery is then," he added.
Elf announced the discovery in water depths of 1,365 metres (corrects from feet), about 200 km (124 miles) north-west of Luanda, last year.
Preliminary tests on one of the wells proved 2,800 barrels per day of good crude through a reduced choke.
Although reports have circulated that the find on block 17 at the Girassol One well are huge, Timbart cautioned that no one knew exactly how big the find was.
"Girassol is a very good well, but that does not mean there is a big field there. We still must assess the discovery," he said.
The test well is being drilled just north of the well at Girassol One, according to Timbart.
Elf Exploration Angola, a wholly owned subsidiary of Elf Aquitaine (corrects details of ownership) is the operator on Block 17 and holds a 35 percent stake.
Other partners on the block are Esso Exploration Angola, BP Exploration (Angola), Den Norske Stats Oljeselskap (Statoil) ), Norsk Hydro with 10 percent and Fina Exploration.
Elf is the second largest foreign oil producer in Angola after Chevron-led consortium Cabinda Gulf Oil Company.
Last year Elf produced about 200,000 barrels per day of crude oil in Angola, Timbart said.
